newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt yields rise amid profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt yields rise amid profit-taking.

text.p: Swedish debt yields rose slightly and the crown firmed against the mark in morning trade on Wednesday.
"The debt market has been performing well these last couple of days and we are now looking at some profit-taking," one dealer said.
The six month T-bill rate increased by one basis point to 4.12 percent and the ten year bond yield rose by three basis points to 7.18 percent.
Sweden's National Debt Office did not lower its forecast for the borrowing requirement for 1997 which some had hoped.
It left the forecast at 20-30 billion crowns while forecasting May's borrowing needs at four billion crowns.
The crown firmed against the mark and dealers said European players were buying crowns against the mark.
The crown was helped by rather positive sentiment surrounding the budget due on April 15 after a number of leaks in Swedish newspapers and by EMU-optimism.
The crown firmed to 4.4700 to the mark versus 4.4760 crowns late Tuesday.
